_comment: Nathan's content queue — the ONLY source of posts. Each poster takes the oldest DUE item with status=pending for its platform and marks it posted. If nothing is due, that workflow posts nothing and exits cleanly.

_fields.status: pending = will post | draft = written, awaiting approval | skip = parked | posted = already sent. Only "pending" is picked up.
_fields.scheduledFor: ISO-8601 UTC. Omit or leave empty to mean 'post at the next slot'.
_fields.text: Telegram: message body (HTML allowed: <b> <i> <a href>). TikTok: the caption.
_fields.imageUrl: Telegram: optional, sends as a photo. Instagram: this OR videoUrl is REQUIRED, and it must be a JPEG on a public https URL.
_fields.videoUrl: TikTok: REQUIRED, public https URL on a domain verified in the TikTok developer portal. Instagram: optional, posts as a Reel.
_fields.author: free text, for your own tracking

items.text:
Most traders react to the Fed without being able to say what it actually is.

It is not one bank and not one job. Five separate mandates, only one of which is the interest rate everyone watches.

Worth knowing which one is moving before deciding a headline matters.

#markets #federalreserve #tradingeducation #macro #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
The "the Fed is a private bank" line survives because the actual structure is rarely shown.

Three branches, split deliberately between a federal agency, twelve regional banks, and the committee that actually votes.

The design is the answer to who controls it.

#federalreserve #macro #tradingeducation #monetarypolicy #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
A failed attempt to corner the copper market ended with a private banker organising a rescue of the US financial system.

That was 1907. There was no central bank to call.

Six years later there was one. Most institutions exist because something broke first.

#financialhistory #federalreserve #macro #tradingeducation #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
A rate decision does not move markets. The gap between the decision and what was already expected moves markets.

That is why price can barely react to a hike, or move hard on a cut that everyone saw coming.

If you are trading the number instead of the expectation, you are reading the wrong variable.

#markets #interestrates #macro #tradingeducation #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
Weak data pushing stocks up looks broken until you follow the chain: softer economy, lower expected rates, cheaper borrowing, support for asset prices.

The part people skip is where it stops working. Past a certain point the earnings damage outweighs the rate relief, and the same news flips sign.

Same headline, opposite reaction, depending on where in that range you are.

#markets #macro #tradingeducation #interestrates #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
Government debt gets discussed as if the number alone means something.

It does not. What it was spent on, what rate was paid, and whether the economy can carry it are three different questions with three different answers.

A large debt at a low rate funding productive assets is not the same thing as a small one at a high rate funding a shortfall.

#macro #governmentdebt #economics #tradingeducation #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
When people say a country is "in debt to" someone, the someone is usually its own pension funds, banks, and households.

Every government bond is simultaneously a liability for the state and an asset for whoever holds it.

The same instrument, read from two ends.

#macro #bonds #governmentdebt #economics #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
A large share of most government debt is held domestically — by pension funds, local banks, and the central bank.

Which makes "owing money to itself" partly true, and the interest a transfer rather than a loss.

It matters because debt owed at home behaves very differently in a crisis than debt owed abroad in a currency you do not issue.

#macro #governmentdebt #economics #bonds #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
The reason printing money does not solve much fits in one line: money is a claim on goods and services, and printing more does not create more goods.

More claims chasing the same output is not wealth. It is a repricing.

Everything else in the inflation debate is detail on top of that.

#macro #inflation #economics #tradingeducation #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
The gold standard is remembered as discipline, and it was — that was the point and the problem.

A hard anchor on money creation is exactly what you want in normal times and exactly what you cannot afford in a banking crisis.

Every monetary system since has been an argument about which of those two matters more.

#financialhistory #gold #macro #economics #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
In 1944, with the war still running, delegates agreed how money would work afterwards.

Fixed rates, other currencies pegged to the dollar, the dollar convertible to gold for foreign central banks. The IMF and World Bank came out of the same meeting.

That is the moment the dollar became the centre of the system — by agreement, not by accident.

#financialhistory #brettonwoods #macro #economics #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
August 15, 1971: the US suspended dollar convertibility into gold.

More dollars existed offshore than there was gold to back them, so the promise was quietly ended rather than tested.

By 1973 major currencies floated. Almost every price you trade today is denominated in the system that decision created.

#financialhistory #macro #forex #economics #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
QE is widely described as printing money and handing it to the public. Neither part is quite right.

A central bank buys assets — usually government bonds — which changes what the financial system holds, not what sits in anyone's account.

Whether that reaches the real economy is the actual debate, and it is a much narrower one than the headlines suggest.

#macro #quantitativeeasing #monetarypolicy #economics #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
A bank can be solvent and still fail.

Solvency asks whether the assets are worth more than the liabilities. Liquidity asks whether it can pay today. A bank passing the first test and failing the second is how most bank runs actually work.

Deposits get lent out. They cannot all come back at once.

#banking #macro #financialhistory #economics #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
The 1929 crash is remembered as the cause of the Great Depression. The sequence is less tidy than that.

Two brutal days in October, then years of banking panics and policy failures that turned a market collapse into an economic one.

The crash did the damage to confidence. What followed did the rest.

#financialhistory #markets #economics #tradingeducation #tradingsocial
items.author: nathan (image) / drafted caption — review before publishing

items.text:
A loss does not prove the decision was wrong, and a win does not prove it was right.

With enough randomness in the outcome, judging yourself on results alone means learning the wrong lesson roughly half the time.

This is why the process gets written down and reviewed separately from the P&L.

#tradingpsychology #tradingjournal #riskmanagement #tradingeducation #tradingsocial

items.text:
A day with no setup still tells you something.

A flat day is not a wasted one — it is a day the market did not offer what you wait for, which is exactly when a plan is worth having.

Patience is a position. It is just harder to log.

#tradingpsychology #tradingdiscipline #tradingjournal #tradingeducation #tradingsocial
